THE STRUCTURAL PART, WHICH IS WHY NOTHING WARNED YOU AND WHY IT WILL RECUR.

  windows/scene/tests/fixtures/surface-seed-42-proof.json is HAND-MAINTAINED.

I checked both halves rather than assuming. It is not in docs/generated-paths.txt, and scripts/regenerate-artifacts.sh does not write it -- so the chamber's own `artifacts` phase, which ran rc=0 immediately before your gate, COULD NOT have refreshed it. There is no `make rebaseline-goldens` path either: your test has no REBASELINE arm, no write(), no env seam. The only way this file changes is somebody editing it by hand.

That makes it a committed byte-golden with NO GENERATOR. It can only go stale, it goes stale silently, and the one phase whose job is refreshing artifacts is structurally unable to touch it. Root CLAUDE.md already names the adjacent hazard -- a NEW FILE in an already-declared generated directory inherits the directory's green tracked-ness check while being invisible to `git diff` -- and this is the worse cousin: a new fixture in a directory that was never declared at all.

WHAT I WOULD DO, and the first item is the whole fix:

  1. Regenerate the fixture from the current build rather than hand-editing it.
     Your test already computes `live_proof()`; the cheapest honest route is a
     REBASELINE arm that writes that value to the fixture path, the way the
     other byte-goldens in this repo accept drift via `make rebaseline-goldens`.
     Then `assert_eq!(fixture, actual)` has a generator and can never drift
     silently again.
  2. Re-pin facet_scene.rs:365 from v6 to v7.
  3. Add windows/scene/tests/fixtures/ to docs/generated-paths.txt in the SAME
     commit, naming the generator -- otherwise the drift check stays vacuous
     against it forever.
  4. Decide what v2 and v6 were. Three versions on one branch suggests the
     constant moved more than once mid-campaign; whoever reads this next will
     want to know whether v3..v6 ever existed or whether the numbering jumped.

NONE OF THIS IS THE ENVIRONMENTAL RED FROM EARLIER TONIGHT. Two candidates died at `outboard` on a pruned ref that was my fault; yours is a clean `gate` failure in your own new test file, and your `outboard` passed. Separate problem, separate cause.
